business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law and Samoan Statute Law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus) (signed 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2004-2012; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018; Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Act 2018.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (beneficial owner, director, shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority (e.g., national passport office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
Certificate of Good Standing for corporate shareholder (if applicable)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN/SSI list, UK HMT sanctions lists, and Samoa's Domestic Counter-Terrorism List published by the Central Bank of Samoa. Enhanced due diligence obligatory for PEPs, non-resident entities, and high-risk jurisdictions; source of funds must be evidenced in all equity holding SPV set-ups.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Company Registration and Name Reservation Portal (sifa.gov.ws), interfaced with the MCIL Companies Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or any language using Latin/Roman script; non-Latin scripts require an English transliteration. Suffix required: 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'S.A.', or 'Pty Ltd' (in practice 'Limited' or 'Ltd.')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 21 days of rejection, accompanied by a submission addressing grounds of repugnancy or conflict. If rejected again, administrative appeal to the Samoa International Finance Authority board, then judicial review in the Samoan Supreme Court. Extension of name reservation is not automatically granted; an application for one further 30-day renewal may be submitted before expiry with justification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible in Samoa for International Companies. A registered agent is required and must maintain a physical registered office at a licensed service provider's address in Apia. The company may use a 'virtual office' for communications and directors' meetings, but actual registered office must be a physical location of the agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% annual probability under risk-based supervision by SIFA and Central Bank of Samoa; higher for companies using nominee shareholders or involving high-risk jurisdictions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1988 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008; key sections: s.5 (incorporation), s.6 (registered office and agent), s.7 (constitution), s.8 (members and shares), s.10 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa, operating through licensed international company service providers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration as an International Company (Form IC-1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and the Registered Agent's consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an International Company; shares may be denominated in any currency, issued at par or premium, and no escrow or capital deposit account is required by the International Companies Act 1988.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the allotment of shares to the initial subscriber be approved and the Register of Members be opened and maintained at the registered office; (2) that the registered office address of the Company as identified by the licensed Registered Agent be adopted, and the agent be appointed to maintain statutory records; (3) that the persons named in the consent forms be and are hereby appointed as Director and Secretary of the Company, each to serve until removal by resolution; (4) that the Director be authorized to open bank accounts, sign banking mandates, issue share certificates, affix the common seal, and execute all ancillary documents; and (5) that all pre-incorporation contracts of the Company be ratified and indemnities granted to officers to the fullest extent permitted by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa via licensed international company service provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance application through a duly licensed international company agent. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must not contain prohibited words, and must include a limited liability indicator. Agent files the Form IC-Name Check and pays the prescribed name reservation fee. The Registry issues a name availability confirmation valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Completed name clearance application
Identity documents of subscribers
Proposed constitutional objects summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit a revised name or file a written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days; the agent may re-file the application without penalty for a non-offending alternative name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed international company service provider and notary public (Samoa or foreign notary acknowledged by Samoa).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, or in Chinese with a certified English translation, containing standard clauses on share capital, restriction of objects, director powers, indemnities, and the election to be an International Company. The subscriber's signature must be witnessed and notarially certified; no mandatory local shareholder presence applies.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notarized subscriber signature pages
Certified English translation if constitution is in Chinese
Consent to appointment of directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If constitutional language is queried, the agent amends and re-executes the constitutional documents; a fresh notarization and re-submission to the Registry is completed within the available SLA window, with no additional Registry fee for non-material amendments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa (electronic lodgment via licensed agent).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent lodges the statutory incorporation package: Form IC-1 signed by the subscriber and registered agent, two copies of the executed constitution, notice of registered office, notice of registered agent consent, and declarations of compliance. The state filing fee of USD 100 is paid through the agent's escrow account. The Registry validations are completed against the name reservation and agent due diligence.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Registration as an International Company)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (2 copies)
Registered agent consent letter
Notice of registered office and registered agent
Subscriber identity evidence and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency query, the agent has 10 business days to cure the defect by filing additional declarations or correcting the form; failure to respond triggers a deemed withdrawal, and a fresh application must be filed with payment of a resubmission fee only where a new name is requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful validation, the Registrar enters the company into the International Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the registration number, incorporation date, and official seal. The certificate is delivered electronically and in certified hard copy to the licensed agent. The company comes into legal existence on the certificate date and the constitution takes effect accordingly.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation application
Registry fee payment receipt
Certificate of Incorporation issuance request (agent transmission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error in the name, date, or registration number, the agent files a rectification request with the certificate and supporting resolutions; the Registrar issues an amended certificate without additional statutory fee within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed international company service provider and Registry of International Companies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent confirms physical registered office premises in Samoa, executes the registered office agreement with the company, and files any final notice of registered office particulars. The agent maintains the statutory records, share register, and register of directors and members, and acts as the point of service for all official communications.
required_dossiers: Registered office service agreement
Registered agent appointment and consent
Final notice of registered office address
Agent due diligence and AML/KYC file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the agent notice due to address or form irregularities, the agent re-files an amended notice within 5 business days; the company remains validly incorporated and the remedy is procedural only without interruption of legal personality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Officer Acceptance, and Commencement of Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company, administered by the licensed agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt a unanimous written resolution to approve the initial share allotment, registered office adoption, officer appointments, banking resolutions, pre-incorporation contracts, and indemnities. Minute the resolution in English, execute the consents by directors and secretary, issue share certificates, and open the corporate bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, and board resolution as the KYC pack.
required_dossiers: First board resolution minutes
Form of consent to act as director and secretary
Share certificate book and initial share certificates
Bank account opening application and KYC pack
Register of members and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking or Registry counterparties query the resolution, the board passes a supplementary ratifying resolution under standard articles; the licensed agent provides a legal opinion on the validity of the first board resolution to satisfy the objecting institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - passive equity holding company with no industrial establishment; registration authority remains the Registry of International Companies, MCIL.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operating, manufacturing, or trading license is required for a pure equity holding SPV under ISIC 6420.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Protection Agency, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical project, construction, or operational facility; EIA registration not triggered for a passive holding vehicle.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the entity has no wastewater, VOC, combustion, or solid waste streams; no discharge or emission compliance threshold applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable - the company holds no physical premises other than the registered office address of the licensed agent and employs no operational staff; fire safety certification, structural load inspection, and workplace clearance requirements are not triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Apia, Samoa; official taxation portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws. The Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA, https://www.sifa.ws) functions as the registry, licensing, and statutory exemption certification authority for all International Companies incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987, operating in coordination with SRA for tax identity matters.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign shareholders establishing a Samoa International Company (IC) must: (1) appoint a licensed international company service provider in Samoa to act as registered agent and maintain the registered office; (2) file the Memorandum and Articles of Association with SIFA under the International Companies Act 1987 and pay the prescribed government incorporation and annual licensing fees, thereby obtaining a Certificate of Incorporation; (3) rely on the automatic statutory tax exemption in section 213 of the International Companies Act 1987, whereby an IC deriving income from outside Samoa is exempt from income tax, VAGST, stamp duty, and all Samoan direct and indirect taxation; the exemption is evidenced by a SIFA-issued Certificate of Good Standing and, upon written request, a Certificate of Tax Exemption; (4) apply to the SRA for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) only where a counterparty bank or intermediary requires a Samoan TIN for KYC/AML or payment routing, using the SRA business registration form together with the IC's incorporation certificate, registered agent resolution, and certificate of tax exemption; (5) confirm that the IC carries on no business, has no place of establishment, and derives no income from Samoan sources, so that no corporate tax registration and no annual income tax return are due to SRA; the IC remains subject only to its SIFA annual renewal and any registered agent compliance obligations; (6) register for VAGST under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2014 only if the IC accidentally commenced a taxable activity in Samoa, which is structurally inconsistent with the pure equity holding SPV mandate and would be a red flag requiring immediate remediation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no foreign-entity 'check-the-box' classification election comparable to United States Treasury Regulation Section 301.7701-3. The offshore tax-exempt status of an IC is automatic and non-elective under the International Companies Act 1987. The only statutorily available elections and transitions affecting tax identity are: (a) conversion of the IC into a domestic company under the Companies Act 2001, which removes the offshore exemption and submits the entity to SRA jurisdiction, income tax at the corporate rate, full 15% VAGST registration, withholding tax obligations, and continuous residence-based reporting, effectively destroying the tax-exempt character; (b) continuance or redomiciliation of the IC to or from another recognized offshore jurisdiction under the International Companies Act, preserving the exemption where the new home regime grants an equivalent zero-tax status; (c) an election to enter the Income Tax Act 2015 group consolidation regime, available only to tax-resident domestic groups and therefore legally unavailable to a tax-exempt non-resident IC; and (d) the hybrid mismatch neutrality election under the Income Tax Act 2015, which similarly only applies to resident entities and cannot be invoked by an IC because Samoa's domestic law does not permit the hybrid entity to opt into tax residency. No special waiver of the 15% VAGST or of corporate income tax can be negotiated; the exemption derives exclusively from the offshore IC statute and is valid only while the IC remains offshore.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 60,000 in annual taxable turnover for compulsory registration; voluntary registration is available under the VAGST Act 2014 once a taxable activity is carried on, even below the compulsory threshold. For a pure equity holding IC, dividend income, interest, capital gains on disposal of shares, and all other passive offshore returns are not supplies made in Samoa, fall outside the charge of VAGST, and are excluded from the turnover calculation for the WST 60,000 threshold. The IC should never hold a Samoan VAGST registration number unless a factual taxable activity in Samoa has inadvertently arisen, which would disqualify the entity from the tax-exempt offshore regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government digital stamping, continuous transaction controls, or API-based electronic invoicing. SRA operates an electronic TIN and returns platform, but paper and digital tax invoices are equally recognized. Where the IC issues a VAGST invoice for any taxable or zero-rated supply (an exceptional event for a passive equity holder), the invoice must contain the statutory VAGST content: supplier name and TIN, recipient name and TIN, invoice date, description of goods or services, quantity and price, total consideration, the VAGST amount or a clear zero-rating declaration, and the registered place of business of the supplier. Invoices must be retained for a minimum period of seven years and be produced to SRA on demand; the absence of an approved electronic clearance system means the substantiation burden falls on documentation integrity, retention, and contemporaneous commercial records rather than on clearance certification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the VAGST Act 2014 applies to: (a) goods physically removed from Samoa in an export transaction, supported by a customs export declaration and transport documents; (b) services supplied to a non-resident person and performed entirely outside Samoa; (c) supplies of international transport and ancillary freight services; and (d) supplies to approved prescribed organizations or in free trade zone arrangements where applicable. A pure equity holding IC is architecturally outside the VAGST system because its core activity (receiving and holding dividends and disposal of shares) is neither a supply of goods nor a supply of services for VAGST purposes; therefore the IC does not need to make zero-rated supplies in the ordinary course. If the IC exceptionally undertakes cross-border trade in goods or supplies offshore services, it may claim a zero rate only upon producing, at the time of filing or SRA audit, customs declarations, bills of lading/air waybills, contracts, bank remittance records, and a contemporaneous zero-rating statement in the tax invoice. Where the IC merely files an annual no-activity confirmation with SIFA and does not register for VAGST, no zero-rating refund claim procedure applies; dividend income and capital gains remain tax-exempt abroad and uncollectible in Samoa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - the electronic or paper export entry processed by Samoa Customs at the port of departure, referencing the IC as exporter of record
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the ocean or air carrier evidencing physical shipment from Samoa to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice and underlying purchase/sale contract describing the goods or services and expressly declaring zero-rated export supply under the VAGST Act 2014
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign exchange credit advice demonstrating receipt of payment in convertible currency from the non-resident customer for the exported goods or services
Packing list, certificate of origin, and such other transport or regulatory export permits as may be required for the particular goods, if the IC ever deviates from passive holding activities
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA audit scrutiny of zero-rated claims focuses on the physical export of goods, offshore consumption of services, genuineness of the non-resident counter-party, and the inflow of foreign currency within a 180-day documentary window. If the IC or any related trader fails the export substantiation test, the zero rate is reversed and the full 15% VAGST becomes payable on the gross consideration, together with monthly late payment interest and a shortfall penalty of 25% of the unpaid tax for inadvertent error, rising to 100% or more of the tax shortfall where the failure reflects intentional disregard, sham documentation, or circular financing. Fraudulent export schemes, false bills of lading, fabricated customs entries, or artificial round-tripping of funds trigger criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 2015 with fines up to WST 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment of up to seven years for directors, officers, and the licensed registered agent complicit in the misstatement. SRA may retrospectively claw back input VAT credits obtained by any related Samoan entity on the strength of the fraudulent zero-rated invoices and may disallow the IC's exemption certificate; SIFA may additionally strike the IC off the register for failure to maintain good standing, and the professional service provider may be deregistered from the international company licensed agents list.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) acting as the Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1974 and the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is partly convertible. Current account transactions are liberalized subject to documentary reporting to CBS and participation of authorized commercial banks, while capital account transactions and remittances by residents require prior CBS approval. Non-resident International Companies (ICs) are generally outside the domestic exchange control net if all transactions are effected in foreign currency and with non-residents. Profit repatriation through the Samoan banking system may still require a Non-Resident Certificate, a certificate of good standing, and CBS approval if settlement is in WST. There is no withholding tax on qualifying dividend distributions from an IC, but dividend remittance to non-residents must be supported by audited financial statements and a board resolution to pass CBS scrutiny. Convertibility risk is low for USD/EUR/RMB/AUD transactions; WST conversion is reserved for domestic-active licensed banks and can be restricted during balance-of-payments stress.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBS Exchange Control Notices issued pursuant to the Exchange Control Act 1974, resident exporters must surrender foreign exchange proceeds to an authorized dealer within 30 days of receipt and convert 100% into WST at the prevailing market rate unless a specific exemption is granted. However, International Companies incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 are exempt from these surrender and mandatory conversion rules to the extent the company does not export domestically sourced goods or settle through the Samoan payments system. For ICs receiving fee income or consideration abroad, proceeds may be retained offshore without surrender. Any direct or indirect inflow into Samoa's domestic banking system of export proceeds for an IC will be presumed surplus to domestic reserve requirements and must be disclosed to the CBS if it exceeds compliance reporting thresholds (typically USD 100,000 per transaction).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (foreign-currency denominated) / Operational Account (multi-currency)
Capital Escrow Account (USD or WST) / Operational Account (foreign-currency settled)
Operational Account (domestic clearing only) / Escrow Account if approved under exchange control exemption

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a principal banking host. Samoa does not have a fintech EMI or digital bank licensing regime; offshore digital EMIs cannot obtain a Samoa banking license or open domestic settlement accounts. They may be engaged as payment facilitators / white-label processors only if such entity holds a Financial Service Provider license under the Samoa Financial Services Authority or operates under a registered intermediary arrangement with a licensed commercial bank. Legal constraints: (i) no passporting rights; (ii) UBO and AML/CFT obligations fall entirely on the licensed Samoa bank; (iii) foreign EMIs must not handle WST-denominated transactions without express CBS approval; (iv) any SWIFT-derived clearing must be done through a corresponding banking relationship to avoid domestic settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for an International Company, subject to a hybrid verification process: at least one director or the Ultimate Beneficial Owner must undertake a face-to-face or live-video interview with the bank's Compliance Officer, and the remaining directors may sign via notarized and apostilled powers of attorney. Evidence of physical substance is not required at account opening, but the bank will require the statutory registered agent in Samoa to provide a Certificate of Good Standing, a Non-Resident Certificate, and a certified copy of the Register of Directors and Shareholders. Some banks retain the discretion to request an in-person board meeting at the bank's Apia branch if the beneficial owner structure is assessed as Medium-Risk-Enhanced (as is the case for a pure equity holding SPV).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or high-risk beneficial ownership jurisdiction with layered offshore intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry excerpts, notarized board resolutions, an annotated group structure chart identifying all UBOs above 10% beneficial interest, passport copies of all directors/UBOs, Certificate of Non-Resident Status issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority, a three-year source-of-wealth affidavit, audited financial statements of the parent entity, and a formal opinion from a licensed Samoa fiduciary validating the economic substance rationale of the SPV.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-like structure with no employees, no physical office, and no clear active treasury activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Group Substance File comprising: management services agreement with a licensed corporate service provider, signed board minutes locating treasury decisions in Hong Kong or Singapore, transfer pricing documentation, evidence of foreign bank account ownership with regular transaction activity, client onboarding due diligence pack for underlying subsidiaries, and a detailed narrative explaining why the SPV is held in Samoa for asset protection and contractual homogeneity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear origin of initial capital injection (unduly large equity for passive SPV)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the transferring shareholder covering at least 6 months, signed gift/equity subscription agreement, tax clearance certificate from the remitting jurisdiction, notarized letter of awareness confirming no money-laundering or terrorism-financing nexus, and a sworn statutory declaration as to the fund origin executed before a Samoa Justice of the Peace if required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols require use of SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through a prime correspondent bank; benefinisary details must exactly match the IC's registered name, the bank beneficiary name, and the amount in the same currency as the subscription agreement. Recommended purpose statements: 'Equity injection into International Company for passive holding of subsidiary shares' or 'Share premium contribution to non-resident international holding entity'. Verification steps: (i) pre-transfer AML screening of the sending account; (ii) CBS notification (Form EC-X) for any WST-denominated inbound transfer exceeding USD 100,000; (iii) if the remittance is in USD/EUR, no CBS approval is needed provided the account is a designated foreign-currency account; (iv) for a capital escrow account, the bank will require an undertaking that funds will be used solely for purchases of participating interests in controlled foreign companies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements comprise (i) direct SWIFT MT103 payments for simple dividend distributions, loan repayments, or service fees; (ii) MT202 cover payments for clearing through Fedwire / CHIPS / TARGET2 when the beneficiary bank is not a direct correspondent; and (iii) commercial letter of credit instruments issued by a Samoan licensed bank using SWIFT MT700 series with reimbursement under UCP600. For trade disbursements tied to third-party acquisitions, a united set of underlying share purchase agreements, valuation reports, and legal opinions will be required to differentiate legitimate treasury movement from shell-company round-tripping. All outbound remittances must cite a reason code (e.g., 'Dividend distribution', 'Guarantee fee', or 'Acquisition of shares') and comply with the beneficiciary bank's anti-money-laundering wire-transmission rules for cross-border transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency swaps (USD-EUR and USD-WST) with an offshore ISDA counterparty
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Samoan Tala (WST) traded through an international bank or prime broker
Plain vanilla currency options (USDEUR, USDWST) transacted under an ISDA and typically requiring a credit support annex
Fully collateralized total return swaps on foreign currency exposures if bankable and consistent with the SPV's passive holding purpose

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Government License Fee (renewal of registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation; the annual license expires on the incorporation anniversary if payment is not made
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 10% of the annual fee per month or part thereof; continued non-payment for approximately 6 months exposes the company to administrative strike-off by the Registrar, consequent dissolution, and loss of limited liability protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Notification (pure equity holding company reduced substance filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of each accounting reference period; filing is aligned with the annual renewal cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate filing fee; failure to file may attract monetary penalties under the International Finance Centre (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019 and referral by SIFA to the Registrar for deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual AML/CFT and UBO Renewal Declaration (customer due diligence refresh)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent (records held at the registered office and subject to Central Bank of Samoa and SIFA inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual renewal date; the agent must receive updated KYC and beneficial ownership confirmations before processing the renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct governmental penalty if completed timely; deficient KYC/UBO documentation delays the annual license renewal and may expose the licensed agent to SIFA licensing sanctions and AML/CFT monetary penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a pure equity holding International Company under the International Companies Act 1987; an audit is triggered only by a members' special resolution, a contractual covenant (lender or investor), the company's constitutional documents, or a specific direction from the Registrar or SIFA
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or another recognized accounting framework selected by the directors; no financial statements need be audited or filed with the Registrar unless the company becomes subject to an economic substance relevant activity or a licensed international banking or trustee regime

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual renewal, the SIFA-licensed registered agent must obtain a written confirmation of the ultimate beneficial ownership, directorate, and shareholding and refresh customer due diligence under the Samoan AML/CFT Act 2018 and Central Bank of Samoa directives. Any share transfer or director change during the year must be notified to the agent contemporaneously and reflected in the private beneficial ownership and statutory registers; there is no public UBO register, but SIFA, the Central Bank of Samoa, and the Registrar may inspect the records on demand.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,000 per annum (standard SIFA-licensed registered agent and registered office service, exclusive of the governmental annual fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–4,000 per engagement (only if a voluntary audit is required by shareholders, lenders, or investors; ordinarily not applicable to a passive pure-equity holding SPV)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for a standard resident Samoan company; 0% effective rate for an International Company (IC) holding a valid tax exemption under the International Companies Act 1987
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory zero-rate exemption for International Companies: no Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, dividend withholding tax, interest withholding tax, or royalty withholding tax on worldwide income and distributions; exemption remains available only while the IC undertakes no domestic Samoan business and maintains its registered agent, registered office, and annual compliance declarations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (IC Act Annual Return) — lodged exclusively through the Lava online registry of the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); no paper filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after each anniversary date of incorporation; the filing date is anchored to the registration anniversary, not to any fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International Company registration number, legal name, and former names
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the exact registration certificate details as issued by the Registrar
Address must be a physical Samoan address maintained by the licensed resident agent; a post office box alone is insufficient

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident agent name, licence number, and countersignature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Samoan licensed agent must verify the identity of ultimate beneficial owners under AML requirements; the agent must remain a natural person or licensed trust/corporate services provider resident in Samoa

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and company secretary: full names, nationalities, residential or service addresses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; at least one director may be non-resident, but the registered agent must retain certified identity documents for each director

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital structure: total issued shares, classes, and shareholder names
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; nominee shareholders must be disclosed to the resident agent with the true beneficial owner identified for the AML file

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance self-declaration applicable to the passive equity holding business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the SPV is a pure equity holder with no employees in Samoa; confirm board minutes are retained and the registered office maintains statutory records
Must be paid by wire from the company account or by the resident agent; payment receipt must be retained as evidence of compliance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial ownership declaration for exchange-of-information purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ultimate beneficial owners must be identified with copies of passports, trust deeds, or corporate charts held by the resident agent; this information is accessible to foreign tax authorities under Samoa's tax information exchange agreements

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late lodgement attracts a fixed penalty typically equal to 100% of the annual fee plus a monthly surcharge calculated per month of default; persistent failure beyond 12 months triggers administrative strike-off by the Registrar, forfeiture of company assets to the Registrar on dissolution, and court-petitioned restoration requiring payment of all arrears, penalties, and restoration fees

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: N/A — no corporate income tax return is filed by an exempt International Company; the Samoa Ministry of Revenue requires only the statutory tax exemption declaration and the annual Registry compliance to be maintained
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Immediately upon any change in shareholders, directors, registered office, or business scope, and in any event not later than 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation; no fiscal-year-end corporate return deadline applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the International Company has not carried on domestic Samoan business during the relevant year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent must provide written confirmation that no Samoan-source trading, ownership of Samoan real estate, or local service provision has occurred

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the International Company's records are physically available in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors must cause copies of accounting records and board minutes to be delivered to the registered office or resident agent

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Loss of the statutory tax exemption with retroactive assessment at the 27% corporate rate, late payment interest, and a concealment penalty of up to 150% of the tax avoided; criminal prosecution is available where false declarations are made knowingly

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company to resident or non-resident shareholders; the general Samoan statutory rate on dividends from a standard resident company is 15%, but the International Companies Act 1987 exempts all IC distributions from withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: An exempt IC does not require Samoan withholding tax relief because the statutory exemption is direct and self-executing. Where treaty relief is sought in a foreign source country, the IC must obtain a Samoan Tax Residence Certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue by demonstrating central management and control in Samoa, including board meetings held in Samoa, local registered agent oversight, and local accounting records; the foreign payer must attach the Tax Residence Certificate to the relief application before the reduced treaty rate is honoured
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoan withholding tax on cross-border interest and royalties paid by a standard resident company is 15%; payments by an exempt International Company are subject to 0% Samoan withholding tax. Under the comprehensive Samoa–New Zealand double taxation agreement, reduced rates generally apply to interest and royalties where a valid Tax Residence Certificate is produced; Samoa's broader treaty network is limited, and source-country tribunals will test substance rather than accept the IC exemption certificate at face value

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold is published in the Samoan Income Tax Act 2012; the Samoa Revenue Authority expects contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where aggregate cross-border related-party payments exceed WST 1,000,000 per annum, while a pure equity holding SPV normally has no intercompany sales and faces documentation exposure only through its parent's Master File and Country-by-Country obligations in the parent jurisdiction
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations apply OECD-aligned substance tests to International Companies operating in geographically mobile activities, including banking, insurance, financing, headquarters, shipping, and IP holding. A pure equity holding SPV qualifies for the reduced substance test: it must maintain a registered office and resident agent in Samoa, keep board minutes and accounting records in Samoa, hold at least one board meeting in Samoa annually, and demonstrate adequate local governance; failure to satisfy the reduced test results in penalties, strike-off, and automatic exchange of information to foreign tax authorities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Abuse of Tax-Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company to conduct domestic Samoan trading, own Samoan land, provide services in Samoa, or otherwise derive Samoan-source income while continuing to claim the zero-rate exemption; filing a false annual declaration or maintaining a second set of books concealing domestic activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive revocation of the tax exemption, assessment at the 27% corporate rate on all concealed income, late payment interest, an evasion penalty of up to 150% of the tax avoided, and a criminal fine of up to WST 200,000; conviction may carry imprisonment of up to seven years under the Income Tax Act 2012
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false declarations are personally assessed jointly and severally where the company is a sham or a facade; the court may issue travel bans, freeze personal assets, and impose disqualification from acting as a director in Samoa for up to ten years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining no physical presence in Samoa, appointing purely nominee directors with no decision-making power, holding no board minutes, keeping no financial records in Samoa, and using the IC solely to disguise ownership of assets in a foreign jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic strike-off by the Registrar under the International Companies Act 1987; restoration of the company requires an originating application to the Supreme Court of Samoa, payment of all outstanding government fees and penalties, and the filing of corrected records; information on the struck-off entity is exchanged with treaty partners without notice to the company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a struck-off company remain personally liable for company debts and governmental fees; the court may pierce the corporate veil on proof of sham, render directors liable for civil restitution to creditors and foreign tax authorities, and prohibit the directors from incorporating a new Samoan entity for up to ten years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Concealment of Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using bearer-like nominee arrangements, failing to disclose the true beneficial owner to the resident agent, transacting with sanctioned persons, or moving funds through the Samoan banking system in a manner designed to obscure the origin of criminal proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act with penalties of up to fourteen years' imprisonment and confiscation of assets; the resident agent that failed to conduct customer due diligence also faces regulatory fines, licence suspension, and criminal sanctions for negligent reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent face criminal prosecution as principals where they knowingly facilitate laundering; courts routinely issue restraint orders freezing personal bank accounts, travel bans pending trial, and disqualification orders; indemnities in the company articles are void as contrary to public policy in money laundering cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Profit Stripping Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mispricing intra-group services, inflating management fees to a foreign parent, basing royalty payments on no underlying IP ownership, or stripping value out of a Samoan taxable subsidiary while the International Company serves only as an invoice conduit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to the arm's length standard under the Income Tax Act 2012, disallowance of excessive deductions, application of the 150% penalty on understated tax, and default interest from the original filing date; the Ministry of Revenue may also issue a direction to re-domicile the foreign parent's service agreements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve fabricated invoices or backdated contracts incur personal civil liability for the tax adjustment where they acted outside bona fide commercial judgment; criminal prosecution for tax evasion is available and includes travel restrictions, asset forfeiture, and imprisonment
